## Welcome

Welcome to the **ICOP 2026 Pre-Conference Workshop** on Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) modeling. This hands-on workshop introduces the Simeoni tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model using Julia and the Pumas ecosystem.

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

- Build mechanistic PK-PD models using the Pumas domain-specific language
- Estimate model parameters from experimental data
- Simulate dose-response scenarios to optimize treatment schedules
- Perform local and global sensitivity analysis to understand parameter influence

---

## Workshop Overview

### The Simeoni Model

The Simeoni TGI model is a mechanistic framework that describes:

1. **Two-compartment pharmacokinetics** - Drug distribution and elimination
2. **Tumor growth dynamics** - Exponential to linear growth transition
3. **Drug-induced cell damage** - Transit compartment model for cell death

This model has become a standard tool for preclinical-to-clinical translation in oncology drug development.

### Why Pumas?

[Pumas](https://pumas.ai) is a comprehensive platform for pharmaceutical modeling and simulation that provides:

- **Expressive DSL** - Intuitive syntax for defining complex models
- **High performance** - Julia-based computation for fast simulations
- **Integrated workflows** - Seamless estimation, simulation, and analysis
- **Sensitivity analysis** - Built-in support for LSA and GSA methods

---

## Session Materials

::: {.session-card}
### Session 1: The Simeoni Tumor Growth Inhibition Model

<span class="time-badge">60 minutes</span>

Learn the biological basis and mathematical formulation of the Simeoni TGI model. Build a complete PK-PD model in Pumas and simulate tumor response across multiple dose levels.

**Topics covered:**

- Exponential → linear tumor growth transition
- Transit compartment model for drug-induced cell death
- 2-compartment PK with micro-rate parameterization
- Pumas model blocks and simulation workflow

[**Go to Session 1 →**](01_SimeoniModel.html)
:::

::: {.session-card}
### Session 2: Parameter Estimation and Dose-Response Analysis

<span class="time-badge">60 minutes</span>

Estimate model parameters from experimental data using the two-stage approach. Explore how dosing frequency affects tumor control through simulation scenarios.

**Topics covered:**

- Additive vs proportional error models
- NaivePooled estimation approach
- Fixing PK parameters for PD estimation
- Dose-exposure-response relationships (Q3W, Q2W, QW, Q4D)

[**Go to Session 2 →**](02_ParameterEstimation.html)
:::

::: {.session-card}
### Session 3: Sensitivity Analysis (LSA and GSA)

<span class="time-badge">60 minutes</span>

Quantify parameter influence on model predictions using local and global sensitivity analysis. Understand which parameters drive tumor growth and treatment response.

**Topics covered:**

- One-at-a-time perturbation (LSA)
- Sobol variance-based indices (GSA)
- First-order (S1) vs total-order (ST) effects
- Parameter interactions and biological interpretation

[**Go to Session 3 →**](03_SensitivityAnalysis.html)
:::

## Hands-On Scripts

All workshop code is available in the `Handson/` directory:

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `SimeoneModel.jl` | Complete model building and simulation |
| `PKestimation.jl` | PK parameter estimation with model comparison |
| `PKPDestimation.jl` | PKPD estimation with fixed PK |
| `SimulationScenarios.jl` | Dose-response scenario simulations |
| `LocalSensitivityAnalysis.jl` | LSA with tornado plots |
| `GlobalSensitivityAnalysis.jl` | GSA with Sobol indices |

---

## Prerequisites

### Software Requirements

- **Julia 1.10+** with Pumas environment
- Required packages: `Pumas`, `PumasUtilities`, `AlgebraOfGraphics`, `CairoMakie`, `DataFramesMeta`, `CSV`, `GlobalSensitivity`

### Background Knowledge

- Basic understanding of pharmacokinetics (compartmental models)
- Familiarity with differential equations (conceptual)
- Some programming experience (Julia or similar)

---

## Reference

**Primary Reference:**

Simeoni M, Magni P, Cammia C, De Nicolao G, Croci V, Pesenti E, Germani M, Poggesi I, Rocchetti M. (2004) "Predictive Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Modeling of Tumor Growth Kinetics in Xenograft Models after Administration of Anticancer Agents." *Cancer Research* 64:1094-1101.
